clue.text: A lounge prepared for 13 on the May the first

explanation.walkthrough: 13 is AMERICAN, the poets' theme: Maya Angelou, whose first name is May followed by the first letter, A.
explanation.definitionFit: Maya Angelou was a celebrated American poet and memoirist, and her forename is MAY plus the first letter of the alphabet.

clue.text: Late Tertiary personality turning up in East Anglian river

explanation.surface: Someone from late prehistoric times surfaces in a Norfolk river.
explanation.walkthrough: The reversed self-image is split round the middle of the river's name, not just placed inside.
explanation.definitionFit: The Neogene is the geological period forming the later part of what was formerly called the Tertiary era.

clue.text: Singular communist editor of Wisden

indicators.note: the name ends like a plural, so making it singular drops its final letter

blocks.note: Friedrich Engels, co-author of the Communist Manifesto

explanation.surface: A cricket almanac's editor is oddly described as a one-of-a-kind communist.
explanation.walkthrough: Wisden is the annual cricket almanac; Matthew Engel edited it from 1993. Engels loses his S as though it were a plural ending.
explanation.definitionFit: Matthew Engel, a Guardian journalist, served as editor of Wisden Cricketers' Almanack in the 1990s and 2000s.

clue.text: When it breaks out, endless weaponry will be used. . .

definitions.text: When it breaks out, endless weaponry will be used. . .

indicators.note: endless means the word loses its last letter
breaking out suggests an eruption that scatters the letters into disorder

blocks.note: the word without its final letter

explanation.surface: A warning that once hostilities start, arms will be deployed without limit.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition, and it runs on into 6 down.
explanation.definitionFit: Open war is undisguised, full-scale conflict, exactly the situation in which every weapon gets used.

clue.text: Observed the end of Man - out of the wood?

dust to dust: mankind ends as dust, as the burial service says

explanation.surface: Someone witnessed the death of mankind and asks whether we are safe now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out of the wood' suggests escaping danger; read literally, it is the powder that comes from cut timber.
explanation.definitionFit: Sawdust is the fine powder produced when timber is cut, literally material coming out of wood.

clue.text: . . .by the military, with a sign about their leader

indicators.note: about means going round, so the sign wraps around the other letter

blocks.note: Aries the ram is a sign of the zodiac
their refers back to the military, whose leading letter this is

explanation.surface: Continuing 4 down: weapons used by soldiers, who rally round their commander's emblem.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue continues 4 down. 'Their leader' is the first letter of military, the word just before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Armies are a nation's organised land forces, so the plural noun stands for the military as a body.

clue.text: Emily the 13 in the back yard like a child?

taken as written

explanation.surface: The poet Emily pictured playing outside in the garden like a youngster.
explanation.walkthrough: 13 is AMERICAN. 'In the back yard' puts IN at the back of the slang word, and a child follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Emily Dickinson was a reclusive nineteenth-century American poet from Amherst, Massachusetts.

clue.text: Having taken a chair, I had a meal which will be enough for me

definitions.note: the clue's verb phrase; satiate means to fill or satisfy completely

blocks.note: sat down on a chair
taken as written
ate is had a meal

explanation.surface: A diner sits down, eats and declares it will do nicely.
explanation.definitionFit: To satiate someone is to supply them fully, giving them as much food as they could want.

taken as written

the last letter of the word for side, closing it round the chain

explanation.surface: A puzzling geography: some territory between sea and river is somehow American.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'Inside' as 'in side': the chain of sea, shortened land and river goes into a word for side, just before its final letter. 13 is AMERICAN.
explanation.definitionFit: Edgar Allan Poe was an American poet and short-story writer, author of The Raven.

clue.text: 13 a tall guy?

explanation.walkthrough: 13 is AMERICAN. The grid gives no link, but this light and 12 across together spell the poet Henry Wadsworth Longfellow, read as 'a long fellow'.
explanation.definitionFit: Long and tall both describe great height or length, and with the next light it names Henry Wadsworth Longfellow.

clue.text: Prevalence in half French town?

explanation.walkthrough: 'French' looks as if it qualifies the town, but it translates the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: Endemicity is the state of a disease being regularly present in an area, its prevalence there.

clue.text: See 10

clue.text: Camera in operation 14 from where we are

explanation.definitionFit: Seen from Britain, where the setter writes, the United States lies to the west, so its people are westerners.

clue.text: Western men with fairy article

the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Cowboys accompanied by a story-book creature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Western' tempts as a film genre with men in it; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Hesperian is a literary word meaning of the west, from Hesperus, the evening star.

clue.text: Attitudiniser after Geller''s model

Uri Geller, the spoon-bending showman
the Model T Ford

explanation.surface: A poser imitating the style of Uri Geller.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Model' looks like an exemplar to follow; it is the Ford car.
explanation.definitionFit: An attitudiniser strikes poses for effect, and a posturist is likewise one who adopts affected postures.

clue.text: A fall guy (9) with a 13 girl

explanation.definitionFit: Roderick Usher is the doomed central figure in Poe's tale The Fall of the House of Usher.

clue.text: Give food and drink to one making decisions about silence

blocks.note: a referee makes decisions in a game

the call for quiet

explanation.surface: Offering a snack to a judge who rules on keeping quiet.
explanation.definitionFit: To refresh someone is to restore them with something to eat or drink, as in light refreshments.

clue.text: Proximity causing many to lose head

taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: 'Lose head' reads as panic, but head is a headland here.

clue.text: Mozart's associate to go to bed in a dress
